brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: Three hex bases piece:0,0,0, piece:1,0,0 and piece:1,-1,0 form a compact cluster, locked with joint bolts (jointBolt at 0,0 slot 1 and 1,0 slot 2). check_build is ok with meshClash clear; only an info-level OPEN_CAP_FACE note remains.

A drawer-frame notch (notch:0#0,-1#notch5, stem hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm) sits in the empty spot beside the touching bases at (0,0) and (1,-1). This is the configurator's drawer-type notch; I did not add a separate drawer part, since drawer offers on a half base were not available in this layout.

requirements.requirement: A spike at a corner where three bases meet
requirements.evidence: Spike spike:0#0,0|1,-1|1,0 (mount variant) sits on the junction shared by bases (0,0), (1,-1) and (1,0).
setSpikeAccessory platform-sm on that mount spike. The solid-type spike refused a platform (TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED), so it was rebuilt as a mount spike, which accepted it.

finish.summary: Built a three-base hex cluster with a drawer-frame notch on one side, a mount spike at the three-base corner carrying a small platform, and joint bolts locking the bases. check_build passes with meshClash clear. Materials, strength and load ratings are not checked by the configurator and are not claimed.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
